```{r setup, include=FALSE}
# ============================================================================
# SYNTHETIC DATA GENERATORS - Slides work without external data files
# ============================================================================

generate_gdp_yield_data <- function() {
  # Generate quarterly GDP and yield curve data (1962Q1 - 2015Q1)
  set.seed(123)
  n <- 213  # 53 years * 4 quarters
  dates <- seq(as.Date("1962-01-01"), by = "quarter", length.out = n)
  
  # GDP: trend + cycle + noise
  trend <- seq(2, 5, length.out = n)
  cycle <- 0.5 * sin(2 * pi * (1:n) / 40)
  gdp_pc <- trend + cycle + rnorm(n, 0, 0.4)
  
  # Interest rates with realistic correlation
  ir3m <- 5 + 0.5 * (1:n)/50 + cumsum(rnorm(n, 0, 0.3))
  ir3m <- pmax(0.1, ir3m)  # Keep positive
  
  ir10y <- ir3m + 1.5 + 0.5 * sin(2 * pi * (1:n) / 60) + rnorm(n, 0, 0.2)
  
  # GDP level (for reference)
  gdp <- 10000 * exp(cumsum(gdp_pc/100))
  
  data.frame(
    DATE = dates,
    gdp_pc = gdp_pc,
    ir3m = ir3m,
    ir10y = ir10y,
    gdp = gdp
  )
}

generate_consumption_income_data <- function() {
  # Generate monthly consumption and income data (1959-2024)
  set.seed(456)
  n <- 780  # 65 years * 12 months
  dates <- seq(as.Date("1959-01-01"), by = "month", length.out = n)
  
  # Income: upward trend with business cycles
  log_pi <- 8 + 0.003 * (1:n) + 0.1 * sin(2 * pi * (1:n) / 120)
  pi <- exp(log_pi + rnorm(n, 0, 0.02))
  
  # Consumption: ~90% of income with slight lag
  log_pce <- log(pi * 0.9) + rnorm(n, 0, 0.015)
  pce <- exp(log_pce)
  
  data.frame(
    DATE = dates,
    PI = pi,
    PCE = pce
  )
}

generate_aids_data <- function() {
  # Generate monthly AIDS diagnoses and deaths (1987-1996)
  set.seed(789)
  n <- 120  # 10 years * 12 months
  dates <- seq(as.Date("1987-01-01"), by = "month", length.out = n)
  
  # Diagnoses: rise then fall with AZT introduction
  peak <- 60
  diag <- 500 + 800 * exp(-((1:n - peak)^2) / 500) + rnorm(n, 0, 50)
  diag <- pmax(100, diag)
  
  # Deaths: lag diagnoses by ~6-12 months
  death <- numeric(n)
  # Start at i=13 to ensure both diag[i-6] and diag[i-12] are valid
  for(i in 13:n) {
    death[i] <- 0.6 * diag[i-6] + 0.3 * diag[i-12] + rnorm(1, 0, 30)
  }
  death <- pmax(50, death)
  
  # Add missingness at start (first year has no/limited death data)
  death[1:12] <- NA
  
  data.frame(
    month = dates,
    diag = round(diag),
    deaths = round(death)
  )
}
```

## Learning Objectives

By the end of this module, you should be able to:

1. Estimate distributed lag and ARDL models with exogenous variables
2. Recognize and avoid spurious regression in non-stationary data
3. Test for cointegration between economic time series
4. Estimate and interpret error correction models (ECM)
5. Forecast using models with exogenous predictors

## Topics

- Distributed Lag Models
- Spurious Regression
- Cointegration
- Error Correction Models

## Motivating Question

Can we use **today's** information to predict **tomorrow's** outcomes?

. . .

Examples:

- Yield curve → Future GDP growth
- Leading indicators → Recessions
- Diagnoses → Deaths (with lag)

. . .

**Challenge**: Both $X$ and $Y$ might be non-stationary!

## GDP and the Yield Curve {visibility="uncounted"}

```{r}
#| code-fold: show
# Load or generate GDP and yield curve data
# If you have the real data, use: tmp <- read.csv("../data/fredgraph (2).csv")
# Otherwise, use synthetic data:
tmp <- generate_gdp_yield_data()

colnames(tmp) <- c("DATE", "gdp_pc", "ir3m", "ir10y", "gdp")
rbind(head(tmp, 5), tail(tmp, 5))
```

## Data Preparation {visibility="uncounted"}

Once you have your data, you might need to add/modify variables.

- Do this *before* converting to a ```ts()``` object.

. . .

```{r results='hold'}
#| code-fold: show
# Create term spread: 10-year minus 3-month rate
tmp$spread <- tmp$ir10y - tmp$ir3m
```

## Data Preparation {visibility="uncounted"}

You can also modify after creating ```ts()``` object:

. . .

```{r results='hold'}
#| code-fold: show
# Convert to quarterly time series starting 1962Q1
tmp <- ts(tmp, start = c(1962, 1), frequency = 4)

# Add spread using ts.union (keeps all columns)
tmp <- ts.union(tmp, spread = tmp[,"ir10y"] - tmp[,"ir3m"], dframe = FALSE)
rbind(head(tmp, 3), tail(tmp, 3))

# Clean up column names
colnames(tmp) <- gsub("tmp.", "", colnames(tmp))
```

```{r include=FALSE}
# Remove duplicate spread column
tmp <- tmp[,-which(colnames(tmp) == "spread")[1]]
```

## Data Manipulation Examples {visibility="uncounted"}

Creating differences, growth rates, and lags:

. . .

```{r}
#| code-fold: show
# ts.union combines time series, aligning by time
head(ts.union(y = tmp[,"gdp_pc"],
              diff_y = diff(tmp[,"gdp"]),              # First difference
              pc_y = 100*diff(tmp[,"gdp"])/tmp[,"gdp"] # % change
              ), 10)
```

## GDP and the Yield Curve {visibility="uncounted"}

```{r results='hold'}
#| code-fold: true
plot(tmp[,c("gdp_pc")], ylim = range(tmp[,c("gdp_pc", "spread")]),
     col = alpha("tomato", .6), lwd = 2,
     ylab = "Percent", main = "GDP Growth and Term Spread")
lines(tmp[,"spread"], col = alpha("dodgerblue", .6), lwd = 2)

legend("topright", lty = 1, col = c("tomato", "dodgerblue"),
       legend = c("%Δ GDP", "Spread (10Y - 3M)"), bty = "n", lwd = 2)
```

## Stationarity Check {visibility="uncounted"}

Always test for stationarity before modeling:

```{r results='hold'}
#| code-fold: true
adf.test(tmp[,"gdp_pc"])
adf.test(tmp[,"spread"])
```

Both series appear stationary (reject unit root).

# Spurious Regression: The Danger

## What is Spurious Regression?

When two **unrelated** non-stationary series appear to be significantly related.

. . .

**The Problem**: Standard t-tests and R² are misleading!

. . .

```{r}
#| code-fold: show
# Simulate two INDEPENDENT random walks
set.seed(123)
N <- 100
y <- cumsum(rnorm(N))  # Random walk 1
x <- cumsum(rnorm(N))  # Random walk 2 (unrelated!)
```

## Spurious Regression: Visualization {visibility="uncounted"}

```{r}
#| code-fold: true
plot(x, y, pch = 16, col = alpha("tomato", 0.6),
     main = "Two Independent Random Walks",
     xlab = "Series X (Random Walk)", ylab = "Series Y (Random Walk)")
abline(lm(y ~ x), col = "dodgerblue", lwd = 2)
text(0, max(y), 
     paste0("R² = ", round(summary(lm(y ~ x))$r.squared, 3),
            "\np-value < 0.001"),
     pos = 4, col = "dodgerblue")
```

**High R², significant t-stat... but they're unrelated!**

## Spurious Regression: Monte Carlo

How often do we falsely reject H₀ when there's **no relationship**?

. . .

```{r}
#| code-fold: show
simulate_regression <- function(N, stationary = TRUE) {
  if(stationary) {
    x <- rnorm(N)
    y <- rnorm(N)
  } else {
    x <- cumsum(rnorm(N))  # Random walk
    y <- cumsum(rnorm(N))  # Random walk
  }
  summary(lm(y ~ x))$coefficients[2, 4] < 0.05  # Reject at 5%?
}

set.seed(456)
nsim <- 1000
```

## Spurious Regression: Results {visibility="uncounted"}

```{r}
# False positive rates
stationary_rejects <- mean(replicate(nsim, simulate_regression(100, TRUE)))
rw_rejects <- mean(replicate(nsim, simulate_regression(100, FALSE)))
```

::: {.nonincremental}
| Data Type | False Positive Rate | Expected |
|-----------|---------------------|----------|
| Stationary (I(0)) | `r round(100*stationary_rejects, 1)`% | 5% ✓ |
| Random Walk (I(1)) | `r round(100*rw_rejects, 1)`% | 5% ✗ |
:::

. . .

**With I(1) data, we find "significant" relationships ~75% of the time even when there's none!**

## Detecting Spurious Regression

**Warning signs:**

1. High R² but low Durbin-Watson statistic (DW < 1)
2. Non-stationary residuals (fail ADF test)
3. Economic theory suggests no relationship

. . .

**Solution**: Test residuals for stationarity!

```{r eval=FALSE}
#| code-fold: show
spurious_reg <- lm(y ~ x)
adf.test(spurious_reg$residuals)  # Should reject if cointegrated
```

## Three Solutions to Spurious Regression

1. **First Differences** (if not cointegrated)
   - Model: $\Delta Y_t = \alpha + \beta \Delta X_t + e_t$
   - Loses long-run information

2. **Cointegration + ECM** (if cointegrated)
   - Captures both short-run and long-run relationships
   - We'll cover this next!

3. **Detrending**
   - Remove common trends first
   - Less common in modern practice

# Distributed Lag Models

## Two Main R Packages {.smaller}

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="50%"}
```dynlm```, ```dynlm()```

- Data can be a ```ts()``` object
- Lags: ```L(var, i:j)``` more intuitive
- No built-in prediction method
- Works with ```stargazer```
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
```dLagM```, ```ardlDlm()```

- Data must be a ```data.frame```
- Lags: ```p``` and ```q``` less intuitive
- Has ```forecast()``` method
- Doesn't work well with ```stargazer```
:::

::::

. . .

```{r results='hide', warning=FALSE}
#| code-fold: show
library("dynlm")
library("dLagM")
```

# ```dynlm```

## Using dynlm()

Main model: ```dynlm()```

- Create lags with ```L()``` function
    - ```L(var, i:j)``` where ```i:j``` is lag vector
    - Can use any vector: ```0:4```, ```c(1,4,8)```, etc.

. . .

Example structures:

- ```L(spread, 0)``` = current value
- ```L(spread, 1)``` = one lag
- ```L(spread, 0:4)``` = current through 4 lags

## Simple vs Distributed Lag {visibility="uncounted" .smaller}

```{r results='asis'}
#| code-fold: show
# Static model (no lags)
r1 <- dynlm(gdp_pc ~ spread, tmp)

# Distributed lag model (current + 1 lag)
r2 <- dynlm(gdp_pc ~ L(spread, 0:1), tmp)

stargazer::stargazer(r1, r2, type = "html",
                     column.labels = c("Static", "DL(1)"))
```

## Alternative Lag Specifications {visibility="uncounted" .smaller}

These three are equivalent:

```{r results='asis'}
#| code-fold: show
r1 <- dynlm(gdp_pc ~ spread + L(spread, 1), tmp)  # Explicit
r2 <- dynlm(gdp_pc ~ L(spread, 0:1), tmp)         # Compact
r3 <- dynlm(gdp_pc ~ L(spread, 0:1), tmp)         # Same

stargazer::stargazer(r1, r2, r3, type = "html")
```

## Choosing Lag Length {visibility="uncounted" .smaller}

Use information criteria (AIC) to select optimal lags:

```{r results='asis'}
#| code-fold: show
r1 <- dynlm(gdp_pc ~ L(spread, 0), tmp)
r2 <- dynlm(gdp_pc ~ L(spread, 0:4), tmp)
r3 <- dynlm(gdp_pc ~ L(spread, 0:8), tmp)

stargazer::stargazer(r1, r2, r3,
                     add.lines = list(c("AIC",
                                        round(AIC(r1), 2),
                                        round(AIC(r2), 2),
                                        round(AIC(r3), 2))),
                     column.labels = c("DL(0)", "DL(4)", "DL(8)"),
                     omit.stat = c("ser", "f"),
                     type = "html")
```

Lower AIC is better. Here DL(4) or DL(8) preferred.

## Aligning Sample Sizes {visibility="uncounted" .smaller}

When comparing models with different lags, ensure same sample:

```{r results='asis'}
#| code-fold: show
# All models should use same time period for fair comparison
r1 <- dynlm(gdp_pc ~ L(spread, 0),
            ts(tmp[9:212,], end = c(2014, 4), frequency = 4))
r2 <- dynlm(gdp_pc ~ L(spread, 0:4),
            ts(tmp[5:212,], end = c(2014, 4), frequency = 4))
r3 <- dynlm(gdp_pc ~ L(spread, 0:8), tmp)

stargazer::stargazer(r1, r2, r3,
                     add.lines = list(c("AIC",
                                        round(AIC(r1), 2),
                                        round(AIC(r2), 2),
                                        round(AIC(r3), 2))),
                     omit.stat = c("ser", "f"),
                     type = "html")
```

## ARDL Models {visibility="uncounted" .smaller}

Autoregressive Distributed Lag: includes lags of both Y and X

```{r results='asis'}
#| code-fold: show
r1 <- dynlm(gdp_pc ~ L(gdp_pc, 1:2), tmp)                    # AR(2)
r2 <- dynlm(gdp_pc ~ L(spread, 0:2), tmp)                    # DL(2)
r3 <- dynlm(gdp_pc ~ L(gdp_pc, 1:2) + L(spread, 0:2), tmp)  # ARDL(2,2)

stargazer::stargazer(r1, r2, r3,
                     add.lines = list(c("AIC",
                                        round(AIC(r1), 2),
                                        round(AIC(r2), 2),
                                        round(AIC(r3), 2))),
                     column.labels = c("AR(2)", "DL(2)", "ARDL(2,2)"),
                     omit.stat = c("ser", "f"),
                     type = "html")
```

ARDL often wins on AIC.

# ```dLagM```

## Using ardlDlm()

Main function: ```ardlDlm()```

- ```p``` = lags of X variables
- ```q``` = lags of Y variable
- ```remove``` = list to exclude specific lags

. . .

Example: ARDL(2,2) with some lags removed

```{r eval=FALSE}
#| code-fold: show
rmv <- list(
  p = list(spread = c(0, 1)),  # Remove spread₀ and spread₁
  q = c(1)                       # Remove Y₁
)
```

## DL(2) Model {visibility="uncounted" .smaller}

Distributed lag with 2 lags of spread, no Y lags:

```{r}
#| code-fold: show
rmv.q <- c(1)                    # Remove Y₁ (keeps only Y₂)
rmv.p <- list(spread = c())      # Keep all spread lags
rmv <- list(p = rmv.p, q = rmv.q)

r1 <- ardlDlm(formula = gdp_pc ~ spread,
              data = as.data.frame(tmp),
              p = 2,   # 2 lags of X (spread₀, spread₁, spread₂)
              q = 1,   # 1 lag of Y (but we remove it)
              remove = rmv)
summary(r1)
```

## AR(2) Model {visibility="uncounted" .smaller}

Autoregressive with 2 lags of Y, no X:

```{r}
#| code-fold: show
rmv.q <- c()                    # Keep Y lags
rmv.p <- list(spread = c(1))    # Remove spread₁
rmv <- list(p = rmv.p, q = rmv.q)

r2 <- ardlDlm(formula = gdp_pc ~ spread,
              data = as.data.frame(tmp),
              p = 1,   # 1 lag of X (but remove it)
              q = 2,   # 2 lags of Y (Y₁, Y₂)
              remove = rmv)
summary(r2)
```

## ARDL(2,2) Full Model {visibility="uncounted" .smaller}

Both Y and X lags included:

```{r}
#| code-fold: show
rmv.q <- c()                    # Keep all Y lags
rmv.p <- list(spread = c())     # Keep all spread lags
rmv <- list(p = rmv.p, q = rmv.q)

r3 <- ardlDlm(formula = gdp_pc ~ spread,
              data = as.data.frame(tmp),
              p = 2,   # Spread: current + 2 lags
              q = 2,   # GDP: 2 lags
              remove = rmv)
summary(r3)
```

## ARDL(2,2) Restricted {visibility="uncounted" .smaller}

Custom lag structure:

```{r}
#| code-fold: show
rmv.q <- c(1)                         # Remove Y₁ (keep Y₂)
rmv.p <- list(spread = c(0,1))        # Remove spread₀, spread₁ (keep spread₂)
rmv <- list(p = rmv.p, q = rmv.q)

r4 <- ardlDlm(formula = gdp_pc ~ spread,
              data = as.data.frame(tmp),
              p = 2,
              q = 2,
              remove = rmv)
summary(r4)
```

Model: $\text{GDP}_t = \alpha + \beta_2 \text{GDP}_{t-2} + \gamma_2 \text{Spread}_{t-2} + e_t$

## Granger Causality

Granger Causality: when lags of $X$ predict future values of $Y$

. . .

**Critical distinction:**

- Granger Causality $\neq$ (`r colorize("Causal", "chocolate")`) Effect
- It means: $X$ today predicts $Y$ tomorrow
- Likely direction: Future GDP expectations → Today's spread
    - GDP `r colorize("causes", "chocolate")` Spread
    - Spread "Granger causes" GDP (predicts it)

## Testing Granger Causality {visibility="uncounted" .smaller}

```{r results='hold'}
#| code-fold: show
# Test if spread Granger-causes GDP growth
lmtest::grangertest(gdp_pc ~ spread, tmp, order = 1)
lmtest::grangertest(gdp_pc ~ spread, tmp, order = 2)
```

Reject H₀: Spread does Granger-cause GDP (it predicts future GDP).

# Forecasting with X

## Forecasting Setup

To forecast Y, we need:

1. Fitted ARDL model
2. **Future values of X** (forecasts or assumptions)
3. Forecast horizon h

. . .

```{r eval = FALSE}
#| code-fold: show
forecast(model,
         x,              # Future X values (X_{t+1}, ..., X_{t+h})
         h = 1,          # Forecast horizon
         interval = FALSE,
         level = 0.95)
```

## Forecasting Strategy {visibility="uncounted"}

**Goal**: Forecast 2013-2014 GDP growth

. . .

**Our approach:**

$$\begin{align}
\%\Delta \text{GDP}_t &= \alpha + \sum_{i=1}^{2}\beta_i \%\Delta \text{GDP}_{t-i} + \gamma\text{Spread}_{t-2} + e_t \\ 
\text{Spread}_t &\sim \text{ARIMA}(p,d,q)
\end{align}$$

. . .

**Steps:**

1. Fit ARDL model for GDP
2. Fit ARIMA model for Spread
3. Forecast Spread first, then use in GDP forecast

## Step 1: Fit GDP Model {visibility="uncounted" .smaller}

```{r}
#| code-fold: show
# Create holdout indicator (1 = test period)
c_namez <- colnames(tmp)
tmp <- ts.union(tmp, h = ifelse(time(tmp) >= 2013, 1, 0))
colnames(tmp) <- c(c_namez, "h")
lim <- tmp[,"h"] == 0  # Training data

# Fit ARDL model on training data
rmv.q <- c()
rmv.p <- list(spread = c(0,1))
rmv <- list(p = rmv.p, q = rmv.q)

main <- ardlDlm(formula = gdp_pc ~ spread,
                data = as.data.frame(tmp[lim,]),
                p = 2, q = 2, remove = rmv)
```

## Step 1: Results {visibility="uncounted" .smaller}

```{r}
summary(main)
```

## Step 2: Forecast Spread {visibility="uncounted" .smaller}

```{r}
#| code-fold: show
# Fit ARIMA to spread
sub <- auto.arima(tmp[lim,"spread"])
summary(sub)
```

## Step 2: Spread Forecasts {visibility="uncounted"}

```{r}
#| code-fold: true
# Generate spread forecasts
p <- predict(sub, n.ahead = 8)

# Get actual test period data (first 8 quarters of test set)
test_spread <- tmp[!lim,"spread"][1:8]
test_times <- time(tmp[!lim,])[1:8]

plot(tmp[,"spread"], lwd = 1,
     ylim = c(-1, 4), xlim = c(2000, 2015),
     xlab = "Quarter", ylab = "Percentage Points",
     main = "Term Spread: Actual vs Forecast")
lines(test_times, test_spread, col = "dodgerblue", lwd = 3)
lines(test_times, p$pred, col = "tomato", lwd = 3)
legend("bottomright", bty = "n", lty = 1, lwd = 2,
       col = c("tomato", "dodgerblue"),
       legend = c("Forecast", "Actual"))
```

## Step 3: GDP Forecasts {visibility="uncounted"}

```{r}
#| code-fold: true
# Benchmark: ARIMA forecast (no spread info)
r1 <- auto.arima(tmp[lim,"gdp_pc"])
p1 <- predict(r1, n.ahead = 8)

# ARDL forecast using spread forecasts
f <- forecast(model = main, x = p$pred, h = 8, interval = FALSE)

# Get actual test period data (first 8 quarters of test set)
test_gdp <- tmp[!lim,"gdp_pc"][1:8]
test_times <- time(tmp[!lim,])[1:8]

plot(tmp[,"gdp_pc"], ylim = c(-2, 3), xlim = c(2000, 2015),
     xlab = "Quarter", ylab = "Percentage Points",
     main = "GDP Growth: Forecast Comparison")
lines(test_times, test_gdp, col = "dodgerblue", lwd = 3)
lines(test_times, f$forecasts, col = "tomato", lwd = 3)
lines(test_times, as.numeric(p1$pred), col = "mediumseagreen", lwd = 3)
legend("bottomright", bty = "n", lty = 1, lwd = 2,
       col = c("tomato", "mediumseagreen", "dodgerblue"),
       legend = c("ARDL (w/ Spread)", "ARIMA", "Actual"))
```

ARDL with spread information outperforms pure ARIMA!

## Alternative: auto.arima with xreg {visibility="uncounted"}

```auto.arima``` can also use external regressors:

```{r}
#| code-fold: show
# Create lagged spread variable
c_namez <- colnames(tmp)
tmp <- ts.intersect(tmp, spread_l2 = lag(tmp[,"spread"], -2))
colnames(tmp) <- c(c_namez, "spread_l2")

# Compare models
r1 <- auto.arima(tmp[,"gdp_pc"])                          # No X
r2 <- auto.arima(tmp[,"gdp_pc"], xreg = tmp[,"spread_l2"]) # With X
```

# Cointegration

## Motivation: The Random Walk Problem {visibility="uncounted"}

## What is Cointegration?

Two I(1) series are **cointegrated** if their linear combination is I(0).

. . .

**Example**: Consumption and Income

- Both trend upward over time (I(1))
- But their **ratio** stays relatively stable (I(0))
- They share a common stochastic trend
- They move together in the long run

. . .

**Key insight**: If cointegrated, there exists a long-run equilibrium relationship!

## Economic Intuition {visibility="uncounted"}

Consider consumption as a fraction of income:

$$C_t = kY_t$$

. . .

Taking logs:

$$\log(C_t) = \log(k) + \log(Y_t)$$

. . .

Rearranging:

$$\log(C_t) - \log(Y_t) = \log(k)$$

If C and Y are cointegrated, the difference is stationary (constant on average).

## Testing for Cointegration {visibility="uncounted"}

**Engle-Granger Two-Step Procedure:**

1. Regress $Y_t = \alpha + \beta X_t + e_t$
2. Test if residuals $\hat{e}_t$ are stationary (ADF test)

. . .

**If residuals are I(0)**: Variables are cointegrated ✓

**If residuals are I(1)**: No cointegration, use first differences ✗

## Consumption & Income Example {visibility="uncounted"}

```{r}
#| code-fold: true
# Load or generate consumption and income data
# If you have real data, use: pi <- read.csv("../data/inc_pce.csv")
# Otherwise, use synthetic data:
pi <- generate_consumption_income_data()
pi$DATE <- ymd(pi$DATE)

par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
# Levels
plot(pi$DATE, pi$PI, type = "l",
     ylim = range(pi$PI, pi$PCE),
     xlab = "Date", ylab = "$",
     main = "Levels",
     col = "tomato")
lines(pi$DATE, pi$PCE, col = "dodgerblue")
legend("topleft", legend = c("Income", "Consumption"),
       col = c("tomato", "dodgerblue"), lty = 1, bty = "n")

# Logs
plot(pi$DATE, log(pi$PI), type = "l",
     ylim = log(range(pi$PI, pi$PCE)),
     xlab = "Date", ylab = "log($)",
     main = "Logs",
     col = "tomato")
lines(pi$DATE, log(pi$PCE), col = "dodgerblue")
legend("topleft", legend = c("Income", "Consumption"),
       col = c("tomato", "dodgerblue"), lty = 1, bty = "n")
```

## Step 1: Estimate Cointegrating Regression {visibility="uncounted" .smaller}

```{r}
#| code-fold: show
# Long-run relationship in logs
reg <- lm(log(PCE) ~ log(PI), data = pi)
summary(reg)
```

Long-run consumption elasticity ≈ 0.99 (nearly dollar-for-dollar).

## Step 2: Check Residuals {visibility="uncounted"}

```{r}
#| code-fold: true
plot(pi$DATE, reg$residuals,
     xlab = "Time", ylab = "Residual",
     main = "Deviation from Long-Run Equilibrium",
     type = "l", col = "tomato")
abline(h = 0, lty = 2)
```

Residuals show mean reversion → suggests cointegration.

## Step 2: Test Residuals for Stationarity {visibility="uncounted" .smaller}

```{r}
#| code-fold: show
# ADF test on residuals
tseries::adf.test(reg$residuals)
```

. . .

**p-value = 0.01 → Reject unit root**

Residuals are stationary → Consumption and Income are **cointegrated**!

# Error Correction Models

## From ARDL to ECM

If variables are cointegrated, we can estimate an **Error Correction Model**.

. . .

**Starting point**: ARDL(1,1)

$$C_t = \alpha + \beta_1 Y_t + \beta_2 Y_{t-1} + \gamma C_{t-1} + e_t$$

. . .

**Long-run equilibrium**: When $C_t = C_{t-1} = C^*$ and $Y_t = Y_{t-1} = Y^*$:

$$C^* = \frac{\alpha + (\beta_1 + \beta_2)Y^*}{1 - \gamma}$$

## Reparameterization to ECM {visibility="uncounted" .smaller}

From ARDL form:

$$C_t = \alpha + \beta_1 Y_t + \beta_2 Y_{t-1} + \gamma C_{t-1} + e_t$$

. . .

Subtract $C_{t-1}$ from both sides:

$$\Delta C_t = \alpha + \beta_1 Y_t + \beta_2 Y_{t-1} + (\gamma - 1) C_{t-1} + e_t$$

. . .

Add and subtract $\beta_1 Y_{t-1}$:

$$\Delta C_t = \alpha + \beta_1(Y_t - Y_{t-1}) + (\beta_1 + \beta_2)Y_{t-1} + (\gamma - 1)C_{t-1} + e_t$$

. . .

Rearrange:

$$\Delta C_t = \alpha + \beta_1 \Delta Y_t + (\gamma - 1)[C_{t-1} - \frac{\beta_1 + \beta_2}{1-\gamma}Y_{t-1}] + e_t$$

## ECM Interpretation {visibility="uncounted"}

$$\Delta C_t = \beta_1 \Delta Y_t + \delta[C_{t-1} - \theta Y_{t-1}] + \text{constant} + e_t$$

. . .

**Two components:**

1. **Short-run dynamics**: $\beta_1 \Delta Y_t$ 
   - Immediate response to income changes

2. **Error correction**: $\delta[C_{t-1} - \theta Y_{t-1}]$
   - $\delta < 0$: restores equilibrium
   - Larger $|\delta|$ → faster adjustment
   - $C_{t-1} - \theta Y_{t-1}$ = deviation from equilibrium

## Estimating ECM {visibility="uncounted"}

```{r}
#| code-fold: show
# Prepare time series data
pi_ts <- ts(pi, start = c(1959, 1), frequency = 12)

# Create differences and error correction term
pi_ts <- ts.intersect(pi_ts,
                      pc = diff(log(pi_ts[,"PCE"])),    # ΔC
                      pi = diff(log(pi_ts[,"PI"])),     # ΔY
                      z = reg$residuals[2:length(reg$residuals)]) # EC term

colnames(pi_ts) <- c("DATE", "PI", "PCE", "pc", "pi", "z")
```

## ECM Specification {visibility="uncounted" .smaller}

```{r}
#| code-fold: show
# Estimate ECM with dLagM
rmv.q <- c()                              # Keep Y lags
rmv.p <- list(pi = c(),                   # Keep ΔY lags
              z = c(0, 2:12))             # Keep only z₁ (EC term)
rmv <- list(p = rmv.p, q = rmv.q)

ecm <- ardlDlm(formula = pc ~ pi + z,
               data = as.data.frame(pi_ts),
               p = 12, q = 12,
               remove = rmv)
```

## ECM Results {visibility="uncounted" .smaller}

```{r}
summary(ecm)
```

## Interpreting ECM Coefficient {visibility="uncounted"}

$$\Delta C_t = 0.25\Delta Y_t - 0.07[C_{t-1} - 0.99Y_{t-1}] + ...$$

. . .

**Error Correction Coefficient** ($\delta = -0.07$):

- Negative ✓ (restores equilibrium)
- If consumption 1% above equilibrium → next period decreases by 0.07%
- Gradual adjustment back to long-run relationship

## Adjustment Speed: Half-Life {visibility="uncounted"}

How long until half the deviation is corrected?

$$\text{Half-life} = \frac{\log(0.5)}{\log(1 + \delta)}$$

```{r}
#| code-fold: show
delta <- coef(ecm)["z.1"]  # Error correction coefficient
half_life <- log(0.5) / log(1 + delta)
cat("Half-life:", round(half_life, 1), "months")
```

About `r round(half_life, 1)` months to close half the gap to equilibrium.

## Decision Guide: When to Use What? {.smaller}

| Situation | Model | Reason |
|-----------|-------|--------|
| Both I(0) | Standard OLS | No spurious regression risk |
| Both I(1), not cointegrated | First differences | Avoid spurious regression |
| Both I(1), cointegrated | ECM | Capture short-run + long-run |
| Mixed I(0) and I(1) | Reconsider specification | Check theory |

. . .

**Workflow:**

1. Test each series for unit root (ADF)
2. If both I(1), test for cointegration (residual ADF)
3. If cointegrated → ECM; if not → first differences

# Homework: Forecasting AIDS Deaths

## The AIDS Forecasting Problem {visibility="uncounted"}

**Data**: Monthly AIDS diagnoses and deaths (1987-1996)

**Your task**: Forecast 2 years of deaths (1994Q2-1996Q1)

```{r}
#| code-fold: true
# Load or generate AIDS data
# If you have real data, use: tmp3 <- readRDS("../data/aids.RDS")
# Otherwise, use synthetic data:
tmp3 <- generate_aids_data()

tmp <- aggregate(list(death = tmp3$deaths, diag = tmp3$diag),
                 list(month = tmp3$month), sum, na.rm = TRUE)
tmp$death <- ifelse(tmp$death == 0, NA, tmp$death)
tmp$diag <- ifelse(tmp$diag == 0, NA, tmp$diag)
tmp <- tmp[year(tmp$month) >= 1987,]

lim1 <- tmp$month <= ymd("1994-04-01") & !is.na(tmp$death)

plot(tmp$month, tmp$diag, type = "n",
     xlab = "Month", ylab = "Count",
     main = "AIDS: Can Diagnoses Help Predict Deaths?")
lines(tmp$month[lim1], tmp$diag[lim1], col = "black", lwd = 2)
lines(tmp$month[lim1], tmp$death[lim1], col = "dodgerblue", lwd = 2)
abline(v = ymd(c("1993-01-01", "1994-04-15")), lty = c(1, 2))
legend("topright", bty = "n", col = c("black", "dodgerblue"), lty = 1,
       legend = c("Diagnoses", "Deaths"), lwd = 2)
```

## Benchmark Model {visibility="uncounted"}

Naive ARIMA forecast (no diagnoses information):

```{r echo=FALSE}
aids_ts <- ts(tmp[lim1,2:3], start = c(min(year(tmp$month[lim1]))), frequency = 12)
reg1 <- auto.arima(aids_ts[,"death"])
H <- 24
p1 <- predict(reg1, n.ahead = H)

plot(tmp$month, tmp$diag, type = "n",
     xlab = "Month", ylab = "Count",
     main = "Baseline: ARIMA Forecast")
lines(tmp$month[lim1], tmp$diag[lim1], col = "black", lwd = 2)
lines(tmp$month[lim1], tmp$death[lim1], col = "dodgerblue", lwd = 2)
lines(tmp$month[!lim1][1:H], p1$pred, col = "tomato", lwd = 2)
lines(tmp$month[!lim1][1:H], tmp$death[!lim1][1:H], col = "mediumseagreen", lwd = 2)
abline(v = ymd("1994-04-15"), lty = 2)
legend("topright", bty = "n", lwd = 2,
       col = c("black", "dodgerblue", "tomato", "mediumseagreen"), lty = 1,
       legend = c("Diagnoses", "Deaths (train)", "ARIMA Forecast", "Deaths (actual)"))
```

. . .

## Hints for Success

1. **Explore the relationship**
   - Plot diagnoses vs deaths with different lags

2. **Model choices**
   - `dynlm`: Easier for exploration, works with `stargazer`

3. **Don't overfit!**
   - More lags ≠ better forecast
